subject: Alderbridge review pack: enable the document viewer
training_context: Harbor project directory excerpt: partner Alderbridge; workspace workspace.alderbridge.example; task: comment on the shared review pack using your Evercrest guest identity. The directory entry is available from your existing project bookmark.
phishing_technique: Consent phishing with excessive delegated permissions
explanation: The expected task is commenting within one shared folder, but the proposed connector requests access to other files, mail, and continued access outside the review. A plausible synchronization explanation and a familiar supplier identity do not establish authorization for that expanded scope. Treat this as suspected consent phishing: do not accept the connector, and verify it with the project owner and IT through known channels. The label describes the authored attack; the visible evidence establishes an unsafe, unverified permission expansion, not proof of a particular mailbox compromise.
learning_objectives: Identify permission expansion beyond a folder-limited task.
Distinguish application consent from ordinary guest sign-in.
Escalate an unverified integration through independent contacts.

subject: SD-4926: replacement-phone enrollment association
training_context: Service Desk record excerpt: SD-4926, replacement work phone requested by you; status: ready for user enrollment through the employee portal. You have not started the enrollment session. Your existing portal bookmark and employee directory remain available.
phishing_intent: Unauthorized sign-in approval and account access
phishing_technique: IT impersonation and unsolicited MFA approval pretext
explanation: A real pending replacement-phone request makes this credible, but it does not authorize a separate authentication session initiated by someone else. The email asks for approval while the learner keeps the portal closed and explains away a support-workstation identity. Decline the prompt and verify the ticket through the existing portal or directory. The visible From address and ticket reference do not prove authenticity. This is an MFA approval pretext, not necessarily repeated-prompt fatigue.
learning_objectives: Distinguish a pending support task from a sign-in personally initiated now.
Evaluate the action and session identified by an authenticator prompt.
Verify support instructions independently before approving authentication.
email_body:
TRAINING CONTEXT (not part of the email):
Service Desk record excerpt: SD-4926, replacement work phone requested by you; status: ready for user enrollment through the employee portal. You have not started the enrollment session. Your existing portal bookmark and employee directory remain available.

EMAIL MESSAGE:
Hello,

Your replacement phone is ready under SD-4926. We are using the enrollment connector to associate the device with your account before the self-service step.

Please approve the authenticator request when it arrives on your existing phone. It may identify a remote support workstation rather than your replacement handset; that is the connector session used for the initial association.

You can leave the employee portal closed during this step. Once the request has been accepted, reopen the saved ticket and continue with the remaining setup instructions.

If the prompt expires, reply with a convenient time and we can repeat the association while you have the existing phone available.

Thank you,
Device Services
Evercrest Group

subject: SD-4926: next steps for your new work phone
training_context: Service Desk record excerpt: SD-4926, replacement work phone requested by you; status: ready for user enrollment through the employee portal. You have not started the enrollment session. Your existing portal bookmark and employee directory remain available.
explanation: The email continues the independently recorded replacement request and asks the learner to start the session from the existing employee portal. Any authenticator confirmation is tied to that newly initiated sign-in, rather than a support session occurring while the portal is closed. This is legitimate within the supplied context. Verify the actual sign-in origin and action before confirming; the correct ticket number and internal-looking address alone are not sufficient.
learning_objectives: Tie authentication confirmation to the session personally initiated.
Compare a support message with an independently available ticket.
Distinguish ordinary enrollment authentication from delegated approval.
email_body:
TRAINING CONTEXT (not part of the email):
Service Desk record excerpt: SD-4926, replacement work phone requested by you; status: ready for user enrollment through the employee portal. You have not started the enrollment session. Your existing portal bookmark and employee directory remain available.

EMAIL MESSAGE:
Hello,

Your replacement phone is ready under SD-4926. When both phones are available, open your existing employee portal bookmark, select the ticket and choose Enroll replacement phone.

The first step asks you to sign in with your Evercrest work identity. Your existing authenticator may then display a request for that sign-in; complete the confirmation for the session you have just opened before continuing to device setup.

After enrollment, the saved ticket will show the new phone awaiting its first test sign-in. Keep the existing phone until that test is complete.

If the old phone is unavailable, use the support contact recorded in the employee directory to arrange the alternative identity check for this ticket.

Thank you,
Device Services
Evercrest Group
